label: Finding equivalent fractions
subject: Mathematics
nextPractice: Make equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same number.

refresher.title: Quick refresher
refresher.body: Equivalent fractions show the same amount. To make one, multiply (or divide) the top number and the bottom number by the same number.

examples.label: Example
examples.text: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 (multiply top and bottom by 2, then by 3)

methods.name: Definition
methods.title: What equivalent fractions are
methods.body: Equivalent fractions look different but show the same part of a whole. To make one, multiply or divide BOTH the numerator (top) and the denominator (bottom) by the same number. Adding the same number to both does not work.

examples.label: Worked example
examples.text: 2/5: multiply top and bottom by 3 → 6/15. So 2/5 = 6/15.

methods.name: Side-by-side comparison
methods.title: Same amount or not?
methods.body: Put two fractions side by side and ask: did the top and the bottom change by the SAME multiplication?

methods.name: Picture it
methods.title: Picture a chocolate bar
methods.body: Picture a chocolate bar cut into 4 equal pieces. You eat 2 pieces: that is 2/4 of the bar. Now picture the same bar cut into 8 equal pieces. To eat the same amount you need 4 pieces: 4/8. Same chocolate, smaller pieces, so 2/4 = 4/8.

examples.label: Same amount
examples.text: 2 of 4 big pieces = 4 of 8 small pieces

methods.name: Step by step
methods.title: Find the missing number step by step
steps: Look at the numbers you know on the same level: 4 on the bottom becomes 20.
Do the same to the top: 3 × 5 = 15.
So 3/4 = 15/20. Check: both numbers were multiplied by 5.

confusions.text: In your test, it looks like the same number was added to the top and the bottom. Adding changes the amount: 1/3 and 2/4 are not equal. To keep the amount the same, multiply (or divide) the top and the bottom by the same number.

keyIdeas: Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same (non-zero) number.
Equivalent fractions represent the same amount or the same part of a whole.
acceptableSimpleWording: I did the same to the top and the bottom
4 goes into 20 five times so 3 times 5
half of the pieces is the same

misconceptionRules.feedback: Your answer is right, but adding the same number to the top and bottom does not keep a fraction the same — multiplying or dividing both by the same number does.

rubric.misconceptionFeedback: Your answer is right, but the reason isn't quite how equivalent fractions work. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number to keep the amount the same.

questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
questions.hint: Multiply the top AND the bottom of 2/3 by the same number. Try 2.
questions.solution: 2/3 × 2/2 = 4/6. Both the top and the bottom were multiplied by 2, so 4/6 shows the same amount.

whyWrong.1: 3/4 adds 1 to the top and the bottom of 2/3. Adding changes the amount — multiply both by the same number instead.
whyWrong.2: 2/6 only changes the bottom number, so each piece gets smaller and the amount changes.
whyWrong.3: 3/2 flips the fraction, which makes it more than a whole. Keep the top on top and multiply both numbers by the same number.

questions.question: Which fraction is NOT equivalent to 1/4?
questions.hint: For each fraction, check: is the bottom number exactly 4 times the top number?
questions.solution: In 2/8, 3/12 and 5/20 the bottom is 4 times the top, so they equal 1/4. In 4/12 the bottom is only 3 times the top, so 4/12 = 1/3, not 1/4.

whyWrong.0: 2/8 is 1/4 with the top and bottom both multiplied by 2, so it IS equivalent. Look for the one where that doesn't work.
whyWrong.1: 3/12 is 1/4 with the top and bottom both multiplied by 3, so it IS equivalent.
whyWrong.3: 5/20 is 1/4 with the top and bottom both multiplied by 5, so it IS equivalent.

questions.question: Which number makes 3/5 = □/10 true?
questions.hint: 5 times what gives 10? Do the same to the 3.
questions.solution: 5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 3 × 2 = 6. 3/5 = 6/10.

whyWrong.0: 8 comes from adding 5 to the top (because 5 + 5 = 10). Fractions stay equal when you multiply, not add: 5 × 2 = 10, so 3 × 2 = 6.
whyWrong.2: 5 doesn't follow a rule here. The bottom was multiplied by 2, so the top must be too: 3 × 2 = 6.

questions.question: Riya ate 4/8 of a pizza. Which fraction shows the same amount?
questions.hint: Divide the top and the bottom of 4/8 by the same number. Try 4.

whyWrong.0: 4/4 is the whole pizza. Only the bottom changed, so the amount changed.
whyWrong.2: 2/8 is only part of what Riya ate: the top changed but the bottom didn't.
whyWrong.3: 8/4 flips the fraction and means two whole pizzas.

questions.question: Which pair of fractions are equivalent?
questions.hint: Look for a pair where the top and the bottom were both multiplied by the same number.

whyWrong.0: 6/7 adds 1 to the top and bottom of 5/6. Adding changes the amount.
whyWrong.1: 2/7 and 4/7 have the same bottom, but 4 sevenths is twice as much as 2 sevenths.
whyWrong.3: 9/3 is 3/9 turned upside down: 9/3 is 3 wholes, but 3/9 is less than one.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 2/7 = ____/21
questions.hint: 7 times what is 21? Do the same to the 2.
questions.wrongFeedback: The bottom went from 7 to 21, which is × 3. Multiply the top by 3 too: 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 5/8 = 15/____
questions.hint: 5 times what is 15? Do the same to the 8.
questions.wrongFeedback: The top went from 5 to 15, which is × 3. Multiply the bottom by 3 too: 8 × 3 = 24.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 12/16 in simplest form is 3/____
questions.hint: 12 divided by what is 3? Divide the 16 by the same number.
questions.wrongFeedback: The top went from 12 to 3, which is ÷ 4. Divide the bottom by 4 too: 16 ÷ 4 = 4.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 4/9 = ____/36
questions.hint: 9 times what is 36? Do the same to the 4.
questions.wrongFeedback: The bottom went from 9 to 36, which is × 4. Multiply the top by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 7/10 = 21/____
questions.hint: 7 times what is 21? Do the same to the 10.
questions.wrongFeedback: The top went from 7 to 21, which is × 3. Multiply the bottom by 3 too: 10 × 3 = 30.
